title: Ability to prevent the user from clearing certain CurrentRefinedValues
body:
I am using instantsearch via the Algolia WooCommerce plugin in a WordPress website.  On product category pages - for instance the user navigates to Clothing > Mens > T-Shirts in the nav - the plugin will use a hierarchicalMenu widget to refine the list of products to those which match the current navigation category.  This is done on init via the code:
`
if(algolia.woocommerce.page === 'category') {
    options.helper.toggleRefine('taxonomies_hierarchical.product_cat.lvl0', algolia.woocommerce.category);
}
`
This refinement is then displayed in the sidebar as part of the currentRefinedValues widget, and other widgets are also displayed for selecting additional faceted refinements.

The problem I'm having is that within the currentRefinedValues widget, if the user clicks on the refined-values item, or clicks on "clear all", then they will still be in the "Clothing > Mens > T-Shirts" area of the site, but they will be faced with products from all categories, which is confusing.

I would like a way to allow users to add new refinements to the search, and to "clear all" of those new refinements, but for the hierarchical refinement which was automatically selected to be hidden, or be read-only.

Looking at the currentRefinedValues component, the template is **always** wrapped in a 'div' and an 'a' tag.  Through the template or the transformData props, I can make the refinement item's _content_ disappear, but the anchor element remains, and the user can click in the space where the element should appear, causing the refinement to be cleared.

If there is some way to achieve my goal with the current code, please let me know.  Otherwise, please consider this feature request.
